finding.claim: The /rss route fetches an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL with no validation and reflects the first 400 bytes of the response.

trace.note: params[:u] is passed unmodified to URI.open, which performs the outbound request and reads the body
data[0, 400] returns the first 400 bytes of the response to the caller

finding.guards_checked: None. No scheme allowlist, host allowlist, private/loopback/link-local IP check, port restriction, or redirect control. open-uri follows redirects by default. Possible file: scheme access via open-uri is not verified by execution.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:7-10 has no validation on the /rss path. The TRUSTED host check at app.rb:14 is only in the separate /trusted route and does not apply to /rss.
verdict.reason: The /rss handler passes the unvalidated params[:u] to URI.open at app.rb:8 and returns the first 400 bytes of the response at app.rb:9, so any unauthenticated caller can make the server fetch an arbitrary URL. The only host allowlist (app.rb:14) sits on /trusted, not /rss. The candidate's file: scheme note was not verified, but the HTTP SSRF claim stands on its own.

finding.claim: The /trusted route makes a server-side GET to any port and path on an allowlisted host. The check is host-name only, so the residual exposure is any port on feeds.example.net or news.example.net, with the full body returned.

trace.note: halt 400 unless TRUSTED.include?(uri.host): exact host allowlist check
Net::HTTP.get(uri) fetches the URL and returns the full body

finding.guards_checked: Host allowlist at app.rb:14 (exact match on uri.host). Bypass attempts checked: userinfo confusion (http://feeds.example.net@evil.com) rejected because host is evil.com; backslash form raises InvalidURIError (500, not a bypass); uppercase or trailing-dot hosts fail closed; missing scheme gives nil host and is rejected; Net::HTTP.get does not follow redirects. Not guarded: port, path, resolved IP (checked by name only). Impact limited to the allowlisted hosts unless their DNS or ownership is compromised or they proxy to internal resources.

verdict.guard_found: Exact hostname set membership on the parsed host at app.rb:14 (`halt 400, "no" unless TRUSTED.include?(uri.host)`, with TRUSTED defined at app.rb:5 as the two-element frozen list feeds.example.net and news.example.net). This is the closing guard the rubric names: exact membership on the parsed hostname.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (app.rb:12-15 match the description, and params[:u] at app.rb:13 is attacker-controlled on an unauthenticated route), but the exact-match host allowlist at app.rb:14 against TRUSTED (app.rb:5) closes the SSRF to arbitrary hosts, so only the non-finding residual of any port or path on those two allowlisted hosts remains, which the rubric does not count as a finding.
